edges.description: Granulomatous inflammation around eggs trapped in the bladder and urogenital tissues produces urogenital inflammation and scarring.
Persistent egg-driven inflammation and scarring of the bladder wall is the chronic mucosal injury on which squamous-cell carcinoma arises.
Chronic S. haematobium-driven bladder mucosal injury is strongly associated with malignant transformation to squamous-cell carcinoma of the bladder.

evidence.snippet: Squamous-cell carcinoma of the bladder is also strongly associated with S haematobium infection.
This tumour is often multifocal, and in regions endemic for S haematobium, occurs at a younger age than do transitional-cell bladder carcinomas.

nodes.description: Persistent inflammation and fibrosis of the bladder wall produced by S. haematobium eggs lodged there over years of infection. It is the chronic bladder lesion on which squamous-cell carcinoma arises; the carcinoma is often multifocal and, in endemic regions, presents at a younger age than transitional-cell bladder carcinoma.

nodes.description: Eggs lodged in tissues such as the liver or bladder provoke granulomatous inflammatory responses.

evidence.snippet: Eggs trapped in the surrounding tissues and organs, such as the liver and bladder, cause inflammatory immune responses (including granulomas)

nodes.description: Egg-induced immune responses cause urogenital inflammation and tissue scarring.
